'''Patricia Ann Baird''', {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|OC|OBC}} (11 October 1937 – 7 August 2026) was a British [[medical geneticist]] active in Canada. Her research specialised in the relationship between medical technology and ethics.<ref name="OrderCanada">{{cite web|url=http://archive.gg.ca/honours/search-recherche/honours-desc.asp?lang=e&TypeID=orc&id=5918|title=Order of Canada citation|archive-date=15 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515220239/http://archive.gg.ca/honours/search-recherche/honours-desc.asp?lang=e&TypeID=orc&id=5918}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Patricia Baird was born in [[Littleborough, Greater Manchester|Littleborough]], Lancashire, England on 11 October 1937, the daughter of Harold and Winifred Cainen Holt.<ref>{{cite book|title=The World who's who of women: Volume 10|author=Ernest Kay|year=1990}}</ref> She was educated at the Queen Mary School for Girls in [[Lytham]], Lancashire. She emigrated to Canada at the age of 17 and was accepted to McGill University. She received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1959 and a [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]], [[Master of Surgery|C.M.]] in 1963 from [[McGill University]] in Montreal.

== Career and research ==
Baird was a University Killam Distinguished Professor Emerita, Department of Medical Genetics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medgen.med.ubc.ca/person/patricia-baird/|title=Patricia Baird {{!}} Department of Medical Genetics|website=medgen.med.ubc.ca|language=en-US|access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref> at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chspr.ubc.ca/about/faculty/baird|title=Patricia Baird|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706210541/http://www.chspr.ubc.ca/about/faculty/baird|archivedate=6 July 2011}}</ref> In 1978, Baird became the head of the Department of Medical Genetics, leading the department to become an internationally renowned research institution. She was the first woman to both be named as chair of a clinical medical department and to be elected to the Board of Governors at the University of British Columbia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://orderofbc.gov.bc.ca/members/obc-1992/1992-patricia-baird/|title=1992 Recipient: Patricia Baird – Vancouver : Order of BC|website=orderofbc.gov.bc.ca|language=en-US|access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref> In 1991, she became Vice-President of the [[Canadian Institute for Advanced Research]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.science.ca/scientists/scientistprofile.php?pID=258#person|title=science.ca : Patricia A. Baird|website=www.science.ca|access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref> In 1989, she became the chair of the [[Royal Commission on New Reproductive Technologies]].<ref name="OrderCanada" />

== Personal life and death ==
In 1964, she married Robert Merrifield Baird. Together, they had three children.<ref name="WhoWho" /> She died through [[Medical aid in dying|medical aid]] (MAID) at her home in Vancouver alongside her husband on 7 August 2026, at the age of 88.<ref>{{cite web|title=ROBERT MERRIFIELD BAIRD|url=https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/robert-baird-obituary?id=62195249|publisher=The Globe and Mail|date=16 August 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=PATRICIA ANN BAIRD|url=https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/patricia-baird-obituary?id=62195248|publisher=The Globe and Mail|date=15 August 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Patricia Ann Baird |url=https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/patricia-baird-obituary?id=62195248 |website=Legacy |access-date=16 August 2026}}</ref> She had [[Parkinson's disease]] and had sustained a recent fall prior to her death.<ref>{{cite web|title=Scientist Patricia Baird was a leader in the evolving field of human genetics|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-scientist-patricia-baird-was-a-leader-in-the-evolving-field-of-human/|last=Kirkup|first=Kristy|date=24 August 2026|publisher=The Globe and Mail|access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
In 1992, Baird was recognised as a [[Order of British Columbia|Member of the Order of British Columbia]] (OBC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orderofbc.gov.bc.ca/members/obc-1992/1992-patricia-baird/|title=Order of British Columbia citation|archive-date=10 January 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110110020450/http://www.orderofbc.gov.bc.ca/members/obc-1992/1992-patricia-baird/}}</ref> In 2000, she was made an [[Officer of the Order of Canada]] (OC) in recognition of being "a contributor to science, public policy and the advancement of women".<ref name="OrderCanada"/> In 2001, Baird became a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]] (FRSC).<ref name="WhoWho">{{cite book|title=Canadian Who's Who 2002|author=Elizabeth Lumley|publisher=University of Toronto Press|page=55}}</ref>

Baird was presented the [[Cooper Ornithological Society]] Harry R. Painton Award in 2013,<ref>{{Cite journal|date=29 January 2014|title=Harry R. Painton Award 2013, to Hope M. Draheim, Patricia Baird, and Susan M. Haig|journal=The Condor|volume=116|issue=1|pages=148|doi=10.1650/CONDOR-13-158.1|s2cid=198156460 |issn=0010-5422|doi-access=free}}</ref> along with her co-authors Hope M. Draheim and Susan M. Haig, for their paper entitled “Temporal analysis of [[Mitochondrial DNA|mtDNA]] variation reveals decreased [[genetic diversity]] in [[Least tern|Least Terns]]” published in ''[[The Condor (journal)|The Condor]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Draheim|first1=Hope M.|last2=Baird|first2=Patricia|last3=Haig|first3=Susan M.|date=1 February 2012|title=Temporal Analysis of mtDNA Variation Reveals Decreased Genetic Diversity in Least Terns|journal=The Condor|volume=114|issue=1|pages=145–154|doi=10.1525/cond.2012.110007|bibcode=2012Condo.114..145D |s2cid=19296987 |issn=0010-5422|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* Baird, P. A., & MacDonald, E. C. (1981). An epidemiologic study of congenital malformations of the anterior abdominal wall in more than half a million consecutive live births. ''[[American Journal of Human Genetics]]''.
* Spouge, D., & Baird, P. A. (1985). Hirschsprung disease in a large birth cohort. ''Teratology''.
* Baird, P. A., Anderson, T. W., Newcombe, H. B., & Lowry, R. B. (1988). Genetic disorders in children and young adults: a population study. ''[[American Journal of Human Genetics]]''.
* McIntosh, G. C., Olshan, A. F., & Baird, P. A. (1995). Paternal age and the risk of birth defects in offspring. ''Epidemiology''.
* Baird, P. (2002). Identification of genetic susceptibility to common diseases: the case for regulation. ''[[Perspectives in Biology and Medicine]]''.
